title: Render your first animation video
summary: Create a Studio project, preview its starter, configure video output and render your first MP4.
outcome: A timestamped MP4 in your project’s outputs/video directory.

blocks.text: The generator installs dependencies and opens Studio with the four-second Write animation in src/scenes/Retiam.ts. Complete [your first scene](/first-scene) to understand add, play and wait.

Generated package.json files declare "retiam": "latest". The initial install resolves npm’s latest engine release. The package manager’s lockfile records the installed version, so later installs can reproduce that project until you update its dependencies.

The project includes config.js with every CLI and engine render setting. Retiam includes Puppeteer as a required dependency. Video rendering additionally needs Chrome with WebGPU and FFmpeg on PATH. See [render requirements](/export#cli-preview-and-final-render).

blocks.text: Use the Studio window opened by the generator to inspect the text, camera, Write animation and final hold. The source editor is below the preview; Run or Ctrl/Command+Enter applies and saves edits. Press Ctrl+C in the terminal when finished, then enter the generated project folder:

blocks.code:
cd my-animation
npm run check
npx retiam lint src/scenes/Retiam.ts --json

blocks.text: To reopen Studio later, run npm run dev. If you followed manual npm setup instead, use its scene path, such as scenes/MyScene.ts, in the commands below.
Open config.js and edit the following output fields. Keep its other settings at their generated defaults. maxDuration is in milliseconds.

The command reads config.js from this project folder and writes a timestamped MP4 under outputs/video. Open it and check the first frame, transitions and final state. The [complete config reference](/export#render-configuration) includes all 33 defaults.
4. Override settings for a final render

These flags override width, height, fps and maxDuration while keeping the remaining file settings. For repeated final renders, save the desired values in config.js. If retiam.config.js is also present, the renderer selects it instead of config.js.

Assets should finish loading before their choreography uses them. Offline stepping stabilizes timeline samples; wall-clock media, network responses and unseeded randomness still need deliberate handling.

items: Set fps to 30 in config.js, then render with -f 60 and compare the results.
Add a longer final hold and increase maxDuration, or set it to 0 to render until the scene finishes.
Capture preview snapshots with npx retiam snapshot src/scenes/Retiam.ts --times 1.0,2.2,3.0 --json.

blocks.text: Check the result: The rendered file should show the same intended sequence as the preview. Snapshot times are seconds and approximate wall-clock preview checks. For failures, follow [troubleshooting](/troubleshooting).
Continue with [Build a mathematical explanation](/project-mathematical-explanation). Use the [tutorial index](/tutorials) to choose another project.
